title: The Seven Bridges of Konigsberg
description: Compute each landmass's degree and apply Euler's odd-degree rule to see why the famous walk is impossible.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Graph Database Architecture

educational.learningObjective: Given the Konigsberg bridge layout redrawn as a graph, the learner will compute each landmass's degree and apply Euler's odd-degree rule to explain why no solution exists.
prerequisites: Knows what a vertex and an edge are
Can count connections at a point
learningOutcomes: Compute the degree of a vertex
Apply Euler's rule to decide whether an Eulerian path exists
Explain why geometry is irrelevant to the answer
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a different small graph and ask whether an Eulerian path exists, with the degree counts as justification.

pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Productive failure - learners attempt the impossible task before the rule is given
pedagogical.feedbackType: Degree readout per vertex plus a parity-based recoloring and rule statement
misconceptionsAddressed: That a clever enough route exists if you look hard enough
That the physical layout of the city affects the answer
discussionQuestions: Why is 'you must leave every place you enter' the whole proof?
What made Euler's abstraction away from geography so powerful?
Where else does only-the-connections-matter reasoning apply?
